lead: Microsoft's entry cloud cert. It proves you can explain cloud concepts, the core parts of Azure, and how Azure handles identity, security, cost and governance. No hands-on work is required, and it never expires. A good first step if your unit runs Microsoft 365 or Azure, which most of government does.
objSub: Three skill areas and 11 objectives from Microsoft's AZ-900 study guide (skills measured as of July 20, 2026). Tick them off as you study; progress saves on this device.

cur.label: Jul 2026
cur.note: Microsoft updates the skills list a few times a year and keeps the same exam code. Check the study guide's date before you book. There's no retirement announced for AZ-900.
cur.onote: Official Microsoft skill areas and objectives, in plain words. Microsoft gives weight ranges (25–30%, 35–40%, 30–35%); the bars use the middle of each range.

domains.name: Describe cloud concepts
obj: Cloud computing
What the cloud is; the shared responsibility model; public, private and hybrid clouds; the consumption-based model (pay for what you use); pricing models; serverless.
Benefits of cloud services
High availability and scalability, reliability and predictability, security and governance, and manageability.
Cloud service types
IaaS, PaaS and SaaS, and a real use case for each.

domains.name: Describe Azure architecture and services
obj: Core architectural components
Regions, region pairs and sovereign regions (like Azure Government); availability zones; datacenters; resources and resource groups; subscriptions; management groups, and how they nest.
Compute and networking

Containers vs VMs vs Functions; VMs, scale sets, availability sets and Azure Virtual Desktop; hosting web apps; virtual networks, subnets, peering, Azure DNS, VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute; public vs private endpoints.
Storage

Azure Storage services; access tiers (hot, cool, cold, archive); redundancy (LRS, ZRS, GRS, GZRS); storage account types; moving files with AzCopy, Storage Explorer and File Sync; migrating with Azure Migrate and Data Box.
Identity, access and security

Microsoft Entra ID and Entra Domain Services; single sign-on, MFA and passwordless; external identities; Conditional Access; role-based access control (RBAC); Zero Trust; defense in depth; Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

domains.name: Describe Azure management and governance
obj: Cost management
What drives cost; the pricing calculator; Cost Management budgets and alerts; tags to sort spending.
Governance and compliance
Microsoft Purview, Azure Policy and resource locks: what each one is for.
Managing and deploying resources
Azure portal, Cloud Shell, Azure CLI and PowerShell; Azure Arc for servers outside Azure; infrastructure as code with Azure Resource Manager (ARM) and ARM templates.
Monitoring tools
Azure Advisor, Azure Service Health, and Azure Monitor (Log Analytics, alerts, Application Insights).

extras.title: How Azure nests
rows: Groups subscriptions; policy and access set here flow down
Resources that share a life cycle; can't nest
A VM, storage account, database or network

extras.title: Storage redundancy
rows: Spread across availability zones in one region
LRS here plus LRS in the paired region
ZRS here plus LRS in the paired region
Lets you read the secondary copy any time

extras.title: Which governance tool?
rows: Allow or deny settings: regions, VM sizes, required tags
Who can do what, at which scope
Sort costs and resources by unit or project
Tips for cost, security, reliability and performance

method: Use the three skill areas above. Architecture and services is the biggest at 35–40%.
Do Microsoft Learn's free AZ-900 learning path. It's written by the same team that writes the exam.
Open a personal Azure free account, set a budget alert, create a resource group, a VM and a storage account, then delete the whole group.
Flashcards: one service per card, plus the hierarchy, the redundancy types and the governance tools.
Take Microsoft's free practice assessment until you score 80%+, then try the exam sandbox to see the question types.
tips: Microsoft renames things often: Azure AD is now Microsoft Entra ID. The exam uses the new names.
Policy controls WHAT can be created. RBAC controls WHO can do things. Questions love to mix them up.
Short questions turn on one word, like “zone” vs “region” or “read” vs “restore.”
Microsoft sometimes gives free AZ-900 exam vouchers to people who attend its free Virtual Training Days. Check before you pay.

items: The official skills list and change log.
Exam details, the free learning path and scheduling.
Try the exam screens and question types before test day.
Use a personal account and card, never a government card or work data. Set a budget alert first.
Optional. The free Microsoft Learn path is enough for most people.

quiz.q: Your unit moves its email to a SaaS service. Under the shared responsibility model, which task is still YOURS?
o: Managing user accounts, access and your data
Right. In every model, including SaaS, you own your identities, who has access, and your information.
Patching the email servers' operating system
In SaaS the provider runs and patches everything under the app.
Replacing failed hardware
Physical hardware is always the provider's job.
Securing the datacenter network
The provider owns its physical network in every model.

quiz.q: Which statement describes the consumption-based model?
o: You pay only for the resources you use, with no upfront hardware cost
Right. That's the cloud's operating expense (OpEx) model.
You buy servers up front and own them for five years
That's the capital expense (CapEx) model of running your own datacenter.
You pay the same monthly fee no matter how much you use
A flat fee isn't based on consumption.
You must reserve capacity for three years before using any
Reservations are an optional discount, not the consumption model.

quiz.q: Developers want to deploy their web app's code without managing operating systems or patching servers. Which service type fits?
o: PaaS
Right. Platform as a service (like Azure App Service) runs the platform; you bring the code.
IaaS
With IaaS (VMs) you still manage the operating system and patches.
SaaS
SaaS is a finished app you use, not a place to deploy your own code.
On-premises
That means running your own servers, which is what they want to avoid.

quiz.q: An app on Azure VMs must keep running if one datacenter in the region fails, with the least cost and effort. What should you use?
o: Availability zones
Right. Zones are separate datacenters in the same region with their own power and network.
A second region in the region pair
That protects against a whole region failing, but costs more and takes more work than the requirement needs.
A resource group
Resource groups organize resources. They don't add any resilience.
A management group
Management groups organize subscriptions for policy and access.

quiz.q: What is the correct order from the LARGEST scope to the smallest?
o: Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups, resources
Right. Policies and access set at a higher level flow down to everything below.
Subscriptions, management groups, resource groups, resources
Management groups sit above subscriptions.
Resource groups, subscriptions, management groups, resources
Resource groups sit inside subscriptions.
Management groups, resource groups, subscriptions, resources
Resource groups live inside a subscription, not the other way around.

quiz.q: Data must survive a full region outage, and an app must be able to READ the copy in the other region at any time. Which redundancy?
o: RA-GRS
Right. Geo-redundant storage with read access lets you read the secondary region any time.
LRS
Three copies in one datacenter. A region outage takes them all.
ZRS
Copies across zones in ONE region. A full region outage takes them all.
GRS
It copies to the other region, but you can't read that copy until a failover.

quiz.q: Leadership wants MFA required only when people sign in from outside the unit's network. What enforces that?
o: Conditional Access
Right. Conditional Access applies rules based on signals like location, device and risk.
Role-based access control (RBAC)
RBAC decides what someone can do in Azure, not how they sign in.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services
That provides domain join and group policy for legacy apps.
Azure Policy
Azure Policy governs resource settings, not sign-ins.

quiz.q: A unit needs a private, dedicated connection from its on-premises datacenter to Azure that does not go over the internet. What should it use?
o: ExpressRoute
Right. ExpressRoute is a private circuit through a connectivity provider.
VPN Gateway
A VPN is encrypted, but it travels over the public internet.
Virtual network peering
Peering connects Azure virtual networks to each other.
Azure DNS
DNS resolves names. It isn't a connection.

quiz.q: No one should be able to create resources outside the East US and West US regions. What enforces that?
o: Azure Policy
Right. A policy like “Allowed locations” denies anything created in other regions.
A resource lock
Locks stop deletes or changes to existing resources. They don't control where new ones go.
An RBAC role
RBAC controls who can create resources, not where.
Tags
Tags label resources. They don't block anything.

quiz.q: You need to stop anyone, even an Owner, from deleting a production storage account by accident, while still allowing changes to it. What should you add?
o: A CanNotDelete (delete) lock
Right. A delete lock blocks deletion but still allows reads and changes.
A ReadOnly lock
That blocks deletes AND changes, which is more than you want.
An Azure Policy deny rule
Policy is for resource settings. A lock is the tool for preventing deletion.
Remove everyone's Owner role
It's drastic, and Contributors can still delete resources.

quiz.q: Before deploying anything, you need an estimate of the monthly cost of five VMs and a database. Which tool?
o: The Azure pricing calculator
Right. It estimates the cost of services before you deploy them.
Microsoft Cost Management
Cost Management tracks what you're actually spending after you deploy.
Azure Advisor
Advisor recommends savings on resources you already run.
Azure Service Health
Service Health reports Azure outages and maintenance.

quiz.q: You want to be alerted when an Azure outage affects the regions and services YOUR unit uses. Which tool?
o: Azure Service Health
Right. It reports outages, planned maintenance and advisories that affect your own resources.
Azure Monitor metrics
Metrics show how your resources perform, not Azure-wide incidents.
Azure Advisor
Advisor gives best-practice recommendations.
The public Azure status page
It shows broad outages, not ones tied to your own subscriptions.

quiz.q: Your unit wants to manage its on-premises servers and some servers in another cloud from the Azure portal, applying the same Azure Policy. What makes that possible?
o: Azure Arc
Right. Arc projects servers outside Azure into Azure so you can govern them the same way.
Azure Migrate
Migrate moves servers into Azure. It doesn't manage them where they are.
ExpressRoute
ExpressRoute is a network connection.
ARM templates
Templates deploy Azure resources. They don't manage outside servers.

pbqs.title: IaaS, PaaS or SaaS?
pbqs.scenario: Your unit is moving six workloads to the cloud. Pick the service type for each.

rows.req: Lift and shift a legacy server onto an Azure VM, exactly as it is
rows.why: A VM is infrastructure. You still manage the OS and software.

rows.req: Deploy the unit's web app code to Azure App Service
rows.why: App Service runs the platform; you only bring the code.

rows.req: Move everyone's email and Office apps to Microsoft 365
rows.why: Microsoft 365 is a finished app you sign in to and use.

rows.req: Run the app's database on Azure SQL Database, with no server to patch
rows.why: A managed database is a platform service.

rows.req: Use an online ticketing system that you just sign in to
rows.why: Software you use as-is is SaaS.

rows.req: Build a virtual network with VMs and your own firewall appliance
rows.why: Networks and VMs you configure yourself are infrastructure.

pbqs.title: Pick the governance tool
pbqs.scenario: Each request came from your division chief. Pick the Azure tool that does it. Each answer is used once; four are distractors.

items.text: Give the help desk read-only access to one resource group.
items.why: RBAC assigns a role (Reader) at a scope (the resource group).

items.text: Show the bill split by unit and by project.
items.why: Tags label resources so costs can be grouped by them.

items.text: Block anyone from creating VMs bigger than a set size.
items.why: Azure Policy can deny resources that break a rule.

items.text: Recommend ways to cut costs and fix security gaps on what we already run.
items.why: Advisor reviews your resources and suggests improvements.

items.text: Track this month's actual spending and email us at 80% of budget.
items.why: Cost Management tracks spending and runs budgets and alerts.

items.text: Find and label sensitive data across our storage and databases.
items.why: Purview discovers, classifies and governs data.

pbqs.title: Pick the storage redundancy
pbqs.scenario: Four storage accounts need a redundancy setting. Pick the cheapest one that still meets each need.

rows.req: Test data. Cheapest possible; losing a datacenter is acceptable.
rows.why: LRS keeps three copies in one datacenter, at the lowest price.

rows.req: Must survive one datacenter failing, and the data must stay in one region.
rows.why: ZRS spreads copies across availability zones in the same region.

rows.req: Must survive a full region outage; nobody needs to read the copy until a failover.
rows.why: GRS copies to the paired region, readable after failover.

rows.req: Must survive a region outage, and reports must read the backup copy any time.
rows.why: Read-access GRS makes the secondary copy readable at all times.

keep.text: Microsoft Fundamentals certifications don't expire, so there's nothing to renew.
keep.after: Microsoft still updates the exam's skills list over time. Your cert stays valid either way.

keep.text: No Azure cert is on the DoD 8140 matrix (V3.0). For a coded billet, you still need one that is, like Security+ or Cloud+.
keep.after: AZ-900 is still worth it as a cheap way to learn Azure before the Administrator exam.

keep.text: Check that CG COOL lists the credential before you request funding, and look for a free voucher from a Microsoft Virtual Training Day first.
keep.after: Government work often runs in Azure Government, a separate Azure cloud for U.S. agencies. The skills are the same.
